Tiered memory `TieredMemory`: short-term working buffer (bounded ring of recent items, exact search), long-term store behind the MemoryIndex trait, and consolidation: items move from short- to long-term when evicted; long-term items carry usefulness stats (retrieval count, reward when retrieved) and low-value items are forgotten under a byte budget. handback.t:
## Report: tiered memory and lessons from mistakes

**Status.** `src/tiered.rs`, `src/lessons.rs`, `src/bin/memory_lab.rs` and `results/memory_lab.json` are done. `src/lib.rs` only got `pub mod tiered; pub mod lessons;`. Nothing is committed.

**Test status.**
- `cargo test --release --lib` does not compile in the real crate right now. The 2 errors are in another agent's `src/workmem.rs` (missing `OpenOptions` and `HnswParams` imports). Earlier `src/mesh.rs` was also mid-edit and broke the build.
- I built and tested my modules in an isolated copy of the crate, with only `router`, `hebbian`, `stats`, `memory`, `tiered` and `lessons`. There, `cargo test --release --lib` gives 47 passed, 0 failed. My share is 19 tests: 11 in tiered, 8 in lessons.
- The full lab was run from the same isolated copy. The binary is the same code as `src/bin/memory_lab.rs`; it just did not build in the real tree. Run time was about 11 minutes.

### API

`neural_mesh::tiered`:
- `TieredConfig::new(dim)` has these fields:
  - `short_cap`
  - `long: LongKind::{Flat, Hnsw(HnswParams)}`
  - `forgetting: bool`
  - `byte_budget`
  - `compression: Option<Compression{bit_width, hot_cap}>`
  - `value_halflife`
  - `init_value`
  - `consolidate_every`
- `TieredMemory::new(cfg)` has these methods:
  - `add(id, &vec, meta) -> bool`: returns false for a duplicate id.
  - `search(&mut self, q, k)`: merges the tiers and counts retrievals.
  - `search_ro(&self, q, k)`: same merge, read-only.
  - `search_tiered(&self, q, k)`: same merge, also returns the tier of each hit.
  - `record_outcome(id, reward) -> bool`
  - `consolidate()`
  - `bytes()`
  - `stats()`
  - `item_stats(id)`
  - `meta(id)`
  - `tier_of(id)`
  - `contains(id)`
  - `len()`
- Tiers: a short-term ring with exact scan, a long-term "hot" store, and an optional cold tier of turbovec 4-bit codes with no f32 copy. Cold scores are estimates.
- `value = Σ reward · 2^(-Δtick/halflife)`, starting at `init_value`. `add` is the clock. With no outcomes recorded, value forgetting is exactly FIFO.
- The budget is only enforced when `forgetting` is on. Forgetting removes the lowest-value items first (ties: oldest) until the byte estimate is under budget.
- `MemoryIndex` has no delete, so three removable stores are local to `tiered.rs`:
  - `FlatRm`: swap-remove.
  - `HnswRm`: tombstones, then a rebuild from an f32 shadow copy that is counted in bytes.
  - `ColdTv`: `IdMapIndex::remove`.
- Byte accounting is an estimate: tight allocation plus `ENTRY_OVERHEAD = 88` B per tracked item for stats.

`neural_mesh::lessons`:
- `LessonConfig::new(dim)` has these fields:
  - `k`
  - `min_sim`
  - `weight`
  - `power`
  - `dedup_sim`
  - `track_successes`
  - `prior_rate`
  - `prior_strength`
  - `memory: TieredConfig`
- `LessonStore::new(cfg)` has these methods:
  - `record_failure(vec, agent, tag, text) -> id`
  - `warning_scores(vec, n_agents)`
  - `adjust_scores(&mut self, vec, scores: &mut [f64])`, which does `scores[a] -= weight * warn[a]`.
  - `observe(agent, success)`
  - `after_task(vec, agent, success, tag, text)`
  - `lessons_for(vec)`
  - `bytes()`
  - `len()`
- Warning per agent is `1 - exp(-Σ ramp(sim) · conf)`, where `conf = (hits+1)/(hits+misses+2)`. A lesson is confirmed when its agent is chosen again and fails, and refuted when it is chosen again and suc

**Easy world** (tight groups, flat-all is perfect; kept in the JSON as `tiered_easy_world`):
- value-forget + cold4 @B reaches 0.996±.001.
- value-forget @B reaches 0.889.
- hnsw-all reaches 0.976.

**What the numbers show, and what they do not.**
- The usefulness-value signal beats recency-only forgetting by about 10 recall points on this workload. This workload is built so that a small useful set recurs. Value forgetting still loses on random old queries (0.42 vs flat-all's 0.87). It only wins overall in proportion to how recurrent the traffic is.
- At 25% of the bytes, the cold 4-bit tier recovers most of what forgetting loses. It keeps 16k of 20k items against 4.6k. It costs about 0.3 recall points against exact search here.
- Cold 4-bit codes lost almost no recall in this synthetic data (keep-all + cold4 = 0.872 vs 0.873), probably because high-dimensional Gaussian-mixture groups are easy to rank. Real embeddings may show a bigger loss. I did not measure that.
- Every recall figure comes from synthetic data. The hot-cap result (small is best) is partly an artefact of this: the cold tier is nearly lossless here, so keeping an exact set buys nothing.
- Absolute latencies are only indicative. The small stores are faster only because they scan fewer vectors. HNSW-all measured the same order of latency as flat scan at 20k items.
- HNSW with forgetting is implemented and unit-tested, but I did not evaluate it in the lab.

### Experiment 2: lessons vs router alone

**Setup.**
- `HebbianRouter` with eta 0.05, temperature 0.02, decay 0.001, epsilon 0.02. 8 agents, 6 task types × 4 latent sub-clusters, 1500 tasks per run, dim 64.
- Three failure modes. The mode agent is the type's best agent, and it fails with probability 0.95 in the mode's region.
- Three scenarios:
  - **A**: the failure region is a latent sub-cluster; the router sees only the type.
  - **B**: the failure region is the whole type, so the router can learn it alone.
  - **C**: no failure modes, noise only.
- Pairing: both arms use the same task stream and the same per-task outcome uniforms. The task streams are identical across A, B and C for a given seed.
- Tuning was on seeds 1-8 only, over weight × min_sim, maximising the mean success gain over A, B and C. Evaluation was on paired seeds 31-60.
- Fail-only lessons: weight 0.5, min_sim 0.7, k=8. With successes: weight 4, min_sim 0.7, k=24.
- Selection replicates the router's epsilon-greedy softmax on `HebbianRouter::scores()`, so the lesson adjustment can be inserted. A `Router::select` run gives 0.630 vs 0.633 router-only in A, so the shared path matches.

**Results (30 paired seeds; mean differences vs router-only):**

| arm | success A | success B | success C | repeat-fail A | exposure A |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| router only | .633 | .583 | .719 | .053 | .057 |
| + lessons (fail-only) | +.052 ±.012 | +.035 ±.017 | +.047 ±.018 | +.007 ±.008 (n.s.) | +.008 (n.s.) |
| + lessons, 60-lesson cap | +.052 | +.028 | +.045 | +.002 (n.s.) | +.003 (n.s.) |
| + lessons + successes | +.084 ±.013 | +.045 ±.018 | +.067 ±.016 | −.034 ±.008 | −.035 ±.009 |
| + lessons + successes, 120-item cap | +.041 | −.014 (n.s.) | +.017 | −.031 | −.032 |

- Exposure means the chosen agent is the one whose failure region contains the task.
- For reference, the HebbianRouter defaults (eta 0.5, T 0.05) alone give 0.545 in A, 0.501 in B and 0.596 in C.

**Attribution** (gain in A or B minus gain in C, paired over seeds):
- Fail-only lessons: A−C = +0.004 ±0.019; B−C = −0.012 ±0.022. Neither is significant.
- Lessons + successes: A−C = +0.017 ±0.018 (n.s.); B−C = −0.022 ±0.021 (significant, negative).

### Verdict

**Fail-only lessons.**
- They raise the success rate by about 4-5 points in every scenario, including the one with no failure modes at all (gain +0.047 in C vs +0.052 in A).
- They do not reduce repeat failures: +0.007 ±0.008, not significant.
- So the gain is generic extra failure-driven correction of a sluggish, greedy router. It is not a benefit from remembering recurring failure modes.
- I did not test a router with more exploration or a different eta as a control for that explanation. It is my reading of the C result, not a measured cause.

**With the success-tracking variant.**
- Repeat failures fall by two thirds: 0.053 → 0.019 in A.
- Success rises 8 points in A and also 7 points in C.
- Net gain attributable to the failure modes is not significant (A−C = +0.017 ±0.018).
- In B, where the router can already learn the failure alone, it adds nothing beyond the generic gain.

**Memory caps.** Fail-only works with 60 lessons. The success-tracking variant is hurt by a tight cap in B (−0.014).

**Bottom line.** Lessons give a real, paired-significant success lift of 4-8 points over this tuned router. Most of that lift is not specific to recurring failure modes. The one clearly targeted benefit is the success-tracking variant's reduction in repeat failures.

### Recommended defaults

**Memory index choice** (from this lab plus the earlier `results/memory.json`):
- Up to about 10k items: `FlatRm` or `FlatIndex`. Exact, simple, and 0.2-0.4 ms per query.
- About 10k to 100k items under a tight RAM limit: tiered with `Compression{4-bit}` and forgetting. A `hot_cap` of 5% of the ring is enough here; keep `hot_cap` larger if your embeddings are harder to rank than this synthetic data.
- Latency-critical large stores with plenty of RAM: HNSW (`LongKind::Hnsw`), but budget about 6 KB per vector, plus the shadow copy f32 if you need forgetting.

**Settings.**
- `short_cap` about 5-8% of the expected store.
- `byte_budget` about 25% of the flat footprint; recall held within 0.3 points of flat here with compression on.
- `value_halflife` about 10k ticks. It had no measurable effect in this lab.
- `consolidate_every` about 100.
- Always feed `record_outcome` back. Forgetting without it is plain FIFO, which was worse by 10 points.
- For lessons: `LessonConfig` with `weight` about 0.5, `min_sim` 0.7, `k` 8 for fail-only. For the success-tracking variant use `weight` about 4, `k` 24.
- If you want the targeted repeat-failure reduction, use `track_successes` and do not cap it below roughly 100 items.
